analysis.title: Labor Update: September 2026 NFP Preview
key_insights: MUFG forecasts September 2026 nonfarm payrolls (NFP) at +90k, versus the Bloomberg median of 85k and a 3-month average of 71k.
MUFG expects the unemployment rate to stay at 4.1%, matching the Bloomberg median. An uptick in job losses on the month could push it to 4.2%.

Leisure & hospitality and local government have driven NFP volatility since June. August's strong rebound corrected much of the negative growth in June and July. MUFG expects both to normalize in September.
Steady growth in healthcare, professional & business services, construction and manufacturing supports an overall September NFP range of 70-110k.
A slight drop in participation of workers aged 55 and over, consistent with retirements, could offset better prime-age (25-54) participation and hold the unemployment rate at 4.1%.
The Chicago Fed Nowcast gives the highest probability to the unemployment rate staying at 4.1%, with equal odds of 4.2% or 4.0%.

Base case: a consensus-like print that reinforces the 'stable' labor market narrative is unlikely to move markets much. Momentum from the rates move into the report could still carry a small rally led by the front end, with October hike expectations falling further.
Downside risk: a weaker headline NFP or higher unemployment rate should produce a bull flattening, with the 10Y Treasury rallying on a weaker growth outlook.
Upside risk: a very strong jobs figure would likely produce a bear steepening, driven more by the stronger growth outlook than by added Fed hikes being priced in.

NFP matters less for Fed expectations and the front end than for forward growth expectations. After the large front-end rally before the report, MUFG expects most of the action in belly to intermediate maturities.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Slightly above the 3-month average of 71k and above consensus, consistent with a stable labor market.
Consensus benchmark that MUFG's forecast is measured against.
Recent trend growth, which MUFG's September forecast slightly exceeds.
Unchanged from the prior month. A move to 4.2% is the stated upside risk to the rate.
The level MUFG and consensus expect to be held in September.
The range MUFG sees supported by normalizing leisure & hospitality and local government hiring.

risk_factors: A weaker than expected NFP or a higher unemployment rate would trigger a bull flattening and a 10Y Treasury rally on a weaker growth outlook.
A very strong jobs print would likely trigger a bear steepening on a stronger growth outlook.
Normal month-to-month volatility in job losses could lift the unemployment rate to 4.2%.
Volatility in leisure & hospitality and local government hiring could push NFP outside the 70-110k range.
vol_and_positioning: Rates across the curve have moved at different speeds. The front end is relatively anchored, while the back end has been grinding higher.
A larger than normal rates move, followed by a reversal the day before the NFP report, reduces the odds of a strong reaction to a consensus-like print.
Expectations of an October Fed hike are falling further ahead of the report.

tension_points.bull_case: A very strong jobs report supports a stronger growth outlook and would likely produce a bear steepening, with the move driven more by growth than by added Fed hikes being priced in.
tension_points.bear_case: A notably weaker report (soft headline NFP or higher unemployment rate) would prompt a bull flattening, with the 10Y Treasury rallying on a weaker growth outlook.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A consensus-like print that reinforces the 'stable' labor market narrative is unlikely to elicit a strong market reaction, which would leave the curve move small.
